properties.areaDesc: Gila, AZ
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 31 at 6:07AM MST until October 31 at 12:15PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Gila County in east central Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 1215 PM MST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of Tonto Creek and flood-prone locations is
imminent or occurring. Tonto Creek continues to rise due to excess
runoff from earlier rainfall. Low-water crossings are inundated
with water and may not be passable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 607 AM MST, a streamflow gauge on Tonto Creek north of Tonto
Basin rose above action stage, with a stage height of 5.12 feet
and flow of 2422 cfs as of 515 AM MST. Flooding is ongoing or
expected to begin shortly along Tonto Creek in the warned area.
Please use the Tonto Creek Bridge for all travel across the
creek. Bar X Crossing, and any other low water crossings, will
likely become impassable.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Tonto Basin.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 31 at 5:48AM MDT until November 2 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected to occur.

* WHERE...A portion of south central Colorado, including the
following areas, the Eastern San Juan Mountains, and the Upper Rio
Grande Valley.

* WHEN...From late tonight through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone location.
Rockslides will be possible in the mountainous areas. Highway 160
and Highway 17 will likely be significantly impacted by this storm.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Heavy rainfall is expected to fall Sunday and Monday across the
area, leading to elevated concerns for flooding in areas that
have recently received excessive moisture, or have recently
experienced flooding.
- The greatest risk of flooding will be along the Conejos River and
the Rio Grande, including Del Norte and Mogote.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood http://cotrip.org
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 31 at 4:45AM PDT until October 31 at 6:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.5 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Pacific Coast.

* WHEN...Until 6 PM PDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.5 feet above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 03:44
PM on Saturday 10/31. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of
surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 31 at 1:38AM MDT until November 2 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of north central, northwest, and west central New
Mexico, including the following areas, in north central New Mexico,
Far Northwest Highlands, Jemez Mountains, Northwest Highlands and
Tusas Mountains Including Chama. In northwest New Mexico, Chuska
Mountains and Northwest Plateau. In west central New Mexico, San
Francisco River Valley, Southwest Mountains, West Central
Highlands, West Central Mountains and West Central Plateau.

* WHEN...From late tonight through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be
flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Another round of widespread rainfall is expected Sunday into
Monday with rainfall amounts generally between 1 and 2 inches
near and west of the Continental Divide, except near 3 inches in
favored upslope regions of the Tusas Mountains near Chama. This
rainfall will occur over very saturated soils which will increase
runoff. These are also areas that are still recovering from the
last flood event. River rises are likely, but rises are not
expected to be as high as the last flood event. If river flooding
materializes, it will likely continue into Monday evening.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Onshore winds and above normal tides will combine to generate
flooding of low areas along the shore. Do not drive around
barricades or through water of unknown depth. Take the necessary
actions to protect flood-prone property.

High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 30 at 2:19PM PDT until November 1 at 7:00AM PST by NWS Sacramento CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected for elevations above 7000 feet. Total snow
accumulations up to 10 inches, with up to 18 inches at the highest
peaks. Minor accumulations of up to 3 inches possible down to 6000
feet.

* WHERE...Northern Sierra above 7000 feet, including Highway 50 and
Interstate 80.

* WHEN...From 8 AM PDT Saturday to 7 AM PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Plan on slippery road conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Snow levels initially 7000 to 8000 feet
Saturday, lowering to 6000 to 7000 feet Saturday night into Sunday.
Heaviest snowfall expected Saturday evening into Sunday. Light
flurries possible down to 5000 feet on Saturday night into Sunday,
but no accumulations expected below 6000 feet.
properties.instruction:
Check the latest road conditions from Caltrans online at
quickmap.dot.ca.gov or dial 5 1 1.

Be prepared for slippery roads. Slow down and use caution while
driving. If you are going outside, watch your first few steps taken
on stairs, sidewalks, and driveways. These surfaces could be icy and
slippery, increasing your risk of a fall and injury.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 30 at 3:02PM MDT until November 2 at 11:00AM MST by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southwest Colorado, including the following
areas, Animas River Basin, Four Corners/Upper Dolores River, San
Juan River Basin and Southwest San Juan Mountains and southeast
Utah, including the following areas, Canyonlands/Natural Bridges,
La Sal and Abajo Mountains and Southeast Utah.

* WHEN...From late Saturday night through Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, recently burned areas, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations. Low-water crossings may be flooded. Storm
drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- 1 to 3 inches of rain is expected across portions of southeast
Utah and southwest Colorado from Sunday morning through Monday
morning over soils that are still saturated from recent rainfall
and flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.
